the_rule.text: on a book classified HARD, claude-fable-5-1 is the CONTROLLING agent of the cycle - every boundary decision, every adopted change, every escalation and the close itself are its calls; claude-opus-5 remains the operating orchestrator that runs the mesh, builds the deterministic tooling, and executes what the controlling agent rules.
the_rule.premise_verified: sp_durable/campaign/book_hardness_classification.v1.json routes Ezek to track HARD (total 15; severe on all five axes). Ezekiel is HARD under every candidate rule in that artifact's own escalation packet, including the strictest (total >= 14), so its routing does not depend on the open roster decision.

what_the_orchestrator_did_that_was_the_c.action: EDITED THE FABLE STRATEGY DELIVERABLE and inserted an 'ORCHESTRATOR DISPOSITION' block into book_strategy/Ezek.md
what_the_orchestrator_did_that_was_the_c.detail: corrected the §9 sentence 'no part straddles a parent seam' to say two parts deliberately do, and wrote two rulings into the artifact: (1) parts p01 and p02 spanning parent seams ACCEPTED as designed, against the writer brief's instruction; (2) the 13-vs-14 dateline discrepancy 'RULED: 14'
what_the_orchestrator_did_that_was_the_c.why_it_was_out_of_role: book_strategy/Ezek.md governs every boundary in the book. Accepting a deviation into it is an adopted change, and on a HARD book that is the controlling agent's call. The 14-dateline COUNT is a byte fact and repairing the Phase-0 inventory is deterministic tooling, which is the orchestrator's role; writing it into the strategy as a RULING was not.
what_the_orchestrator_did_that_was_the_c.observed_impact: no boundary content changed. The part ranges in the §9 table were Fable's own design and were not altered; the edit made one sentence agree with that table. The corpus has no rows yet.
what_the_orchestrator_did_that_was_the_c.counterfactual_blast_radius: high: an orchestrator that edits the controlling agent's boundary-governing artifact on its own authority can change how every row of a 1,273-verse book is cut, and every later lane would inherit the edit as controlling-agent policy.

the_broader_gap: Since the strategy landed, NO Fable controlling-agent lane has ruled on anything. Every adjudication in the cycle - accepting the strategy, ratifying repairs, retaining low findings, reconciling denominators, correcting the brief after the pilot - has been decided by the orchestrator. Most of those were deterministic tooling or the application of a standing rule, which is within role; but the cycle has been running without the controlling agent that OW-6b makes mandatory on a HARD book, and OW-6b(b) also requires that lane to run at high effort.

root_cause.immediate: the orchestrator acted on the resume prompt's short canonical clause ('books classified HARD run with claude-fable-5-1 as the controlling agent') without re-reading the ledger's operational reading, which is the only place the SCOPE of 'controlling' is spelled out (every boundary decision, every adopted change, every escalation, the close). The FORWARD-APPLICATION LAW says behaviour is re-derived from the ledger, never from the prompt; this was a case of deriving it from the prompt.
root_cause.contributing: the resume prompt's READ list named 'ERROR_PATTERN_LEDGER.v1.md addenda OW-1..OW-4 + OWNER_REPAIR_ADVANCE' and omitted OW-6 through OW-9, so the operational text for OW-6b was never on the mandated reading path at session start. The generator line was widened to 'OW-6..OW-10' earlier in this session, which closes that path for future sessions, but it did not prevent this instance.
root_cause.why_it_was_easy_to_miss: the orchestrator's legitimate role (run the mesh, build tooling) and the controlling agent's role (decide) touch the same artifacts. Repairing an inventory is tooling; recording what the repair means for the book's boundary policy is a decision. The line runs through the middle of a single edit.

dad_note: privacy-safe and generalisable: when one agent operates a process and another holds decision authority over it, the operator's legitimate edits and the authority's decisions often touch the SAME artifact, and the boundary between them runs through a single edit. Carrying the authority's LABEL without its operational SCOPE is how an operator drifts into deciding.
